# vapour

## Overview

The vapour package provides access to the basic *read* functions
available in [GDAL](https://gdal.org/) for both
[raster](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/raster_data_model.html) and
[vector](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/vector_data_model.html) data
sources.

The functions are deliberately *lower-level* than these data models and
provide access to the component entities independently.

For vector data:

- read access to fields alone
- read raw binary geometry alone, or geometry in text forms (GeoJSON,
  WKT, GML, KML).
- read access to the extent of geometries
- helper functions to summarize feature identity and geometry status
- limit/skip control on records read
- execution of
  [OGRSQL](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/ogr_sql_dialect.html) with
  control of SQL dialect
- read in the context of a [bounding box spatial
  filter](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/ogr_sql_dialect.html#executesql)
  can be applied via the `extent` argument

For raster data:

- read access to the list of available rasters within a collection
  source (subdatasets).
- read access to *structural metadata* for individual raster sources.
- read access for raw data using GDAL’s [RasterIO
  framework](https://gdal.org/en/stable/tutorials/raster_api_tut.html)
  and its dynamic image decimation / replication resampling algorithms.
- read access for raw data using GDAL’s [Warper
  framework](https://gdal.org/en/stable/api/gdalwarp_cpp.html) and its
  dynamic image warping, a superset of the RasterIO capabilities.

The warper works for data sources that contain *overviews* (or pyramid
levels-of-detail) as it automatically chooses an appropriate level for
the request made, files, urls, database connections, online tiled image
servers, and all the various ways of specifying GDAL data sources.

The workflows available are intended to support development of
applications in R for these vector and raster data without being
constrained to any particular data model.

## Installation

### From CRAN

Install from CRAN, this should work on MacOS and Windows because CRAN
provide binaries.

``` r

install.packages("vapour")
```

### From conda-forge

[![conda-forge
platforms](https://img.shields.io/conda/pn/conda-forge/r-vapour.svg)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/r-vapour)

Vapour is available on
[conda-forge](https://github.com/conda-forge/r-vapour-feedstock) as
`r-vapour` and can be installed with [Pixi](https://pixi.prefix.dev/):

``` bash
pixi add r-vapour
```

or with [`conda`](https://docs.conda.io/):

``` bash
conda install --channel conda-forge r-vapour
```

The conda-forge package installs all its dependencies from conda-forge,
so no system libraries are required.

### Development version

The development version can be installed from GitHub.

``` r

options(repos = c(
    hypertidy = 'https://hypertidy.r-universe.dev',
    CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))
install.packages("vapour")
```

To install the development version the more GitHub-traditional way:

``` r

remotes::install_github("hypertidy/vapour")
```

You will need development tools for building R packages.

On Linux, I’m using latest ubuntu and R usually, check CRAN on ubuntu
(search for “ubuntu cran”).

then

``` bash
apt install --no-install-recommends software-properties-common dirmngr
add-apt-repository ppa:ubuntugis/ubuntugis-unstable --yes

apt update

## Install 3rd parties

## NetCDF and geo-spatial wunderkind
apt install libgdal-dev 
```

then `install.packages("vapour")` or whatever you use.

## Purpose

The goal of vapour is to provide a basic **GDAL API** package for R. The
key functions provide vector geometry or attributes and raster data and
raster metadata.

The priority is to give low-level access to key functionality rather
than comprehensive coverage of the library. The real advantage of
`vapour` is the flexibility of a modular workflow, not the outright
efficiency.

A parallel goal is to be freed from the powerful but sometimes limiting
high-level data models of GDAL itself, specifically these are *simple
features* and *affine-based regular rasters composed of 2D slices*.
(GDAL will possibly remove these limitations over time but still there
will always be value in having modularity in an ecosystem of tools.)

GDAL’s dynamic resampling of arbitrary raster windows is also very
useful for interactive tools on local data, and is radically
under-utilized. A quick example, topography data is available from
Amazon compute servers, first we need a config for the source:

``` r

elevation.tiles.prod <- 
 '<GDAL_WMS>
  <Service name="TMS">
    <ServerUrl>https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/geotiff/${z}/${x}/${y}.tif</ServerUrl>
  </Service>
  <DataWindow>
    <UpperLeftX>-20037508.34</UpperLeftX>
    <UpperLeftY>20037508.34</UpperLeftY>
    <LowerRightX>20037508.34</LowerRightX>
    <LowerRightY>-20037508.34</LowerRightY>
    <TileLevel>14</TileLevel>
    <TileCountX>1</TileCountX>
    <TileCountY>1</TileCountY>
    <YOrigin>top</YOrigin>
  </DataWindow>
  <Projection>EPSG:3857</Projection>
  <BlockSizeX>512</BlockSizeX>
  <BlockSizeY>512</BlockSizeY>
  <BandsCount>1</BandsCount>
  <DataType>Int16</DataType>
  <ZeroBlockHttpCodes>403,404</ZeroBlockHttpCodes>
  <DataValues>
    <NoData>-32768</NoData>
  </DataValues>
  <Cache/>
</GDAL_WMS>'
```

``` r

## we want an extent
ex <- c(-1, 1, -1, 1) * 5000  ## 10km wide/high region
## Madrid is at this location
pt <- cbind(-3.716667, 40.416667)
crs <- sprintf("+proj=laea +lon_0=%f +lat_0=%f +datum=WGS84", pt[1,1,drop = TRUE], pt[1,2, drop = TRUE])
dm <- c(256, 256)


vals <- vapour::vapour_warp_raster(elevation.tiles.prod, extent = ex, dimension = dm, projection = crs)
## now we can use this in a matrix
image(m <- matrix(vals[[1]], nrow = dm[2], ncol = dm[1])[,dm[2]:1 ])
```

![](reference/figures/README-topo-example-1.png)

``` r

## using the image list format
x <- list(x = seq(ex[1], ex[2], length.out = dm[1] + 1), y = seq(ex[3] ,ex[4], length.out = dm[1] + 1), z = m)
image(x)

## or as a spatial object
library(terra)
r <- rast(ext(ex), nrows = dm[2], ncols = dm[1], crs = crs, vals = vals[[1]])
contour(r, add = TRUE)
```

![](reference/figures/README-topo-example-2.png)

If we want more detail, go ahead:

``` r

dm <- c(512, 512)
vals <- vapour::vapour_warp_raster(elevation.tiles.prod, extent = ex, dimension = dm, projection = crs)
(r <- rast(ext(ex), nrows = dm[2], ncols = dm[1], crs = crs, vals = vals[[1]]))
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 512, 512, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 19.53125, 19.53125  (x, y)
#> extent      : -5000, 5000, -5000, 5000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : +proj=laea +lat_0=40.416667 +lon_0=-3.716667 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        : lyr.1
#> min value   :   562
#> max value   :   742
plot(r, col = hcl.colors(24))
```

![](reference/figures/README-lod-1.png)

GDAL is obstinately *format agnostic*, the A stands for *Abstraction*
and we like that in R too, just gives us the data. Here we created a
base matrix image object, and a raster package *RasterLayer*, but we
could use the spatstat im, or objects in stars or terra packages, it
makes no difference to the read-through-warp process.

This partly draws on work done in [the sf
package](https://github.com/r-spatial/sf) and [the terra
package](https://github.com/rspatial/terra) and in packages `rgdal` and
`rgdal2`. I’m amazed that something as powerful and general as GDAL is
still only available through these lenses, but maybe more folks will get
interested over time.

## Examples

The package documentation page gives an overview of available functions.

``` r

help("vapour-package")
```

See the vignettes and documentation for examples WIP.

## Context

Examples of packages that use vapour are in development, especially
[whatarelief](https://github.com/hypertidy/whatarelief) and
[ggdal](https://github.com/rgdal-dev/ggdal).

Limitations, work-in-progress and other discussion:

<https://github.com/hypertidy/vapour/issues/4>

# Package index

## Package overview

- [`vapour-package`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour-package.md)
  [`vapour`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour-package.md)
  : vapour

## Raster information

Structural metadata, subdatasets, control points and geolocation.

- [`vapour_raster_info()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_raster_info.md)
  : Raster information
- [`vapour_sds_names()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_sds_names.md)
  : GDAL raster subdatasets (variables)
- [`vapour_sds()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_sds.md)
  : Subdatasets of raster sources
- [`vapour_raster_gcp()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_raster_gcp.md)
  : Raster ground control points
- [`vapour_geolocation()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_geolocation.md)
  : Retrieve geolocation information for a dataset

## Raster data

Read, warp and create raster data.

- [`vapour_read_raster()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster.md)
  : Raster IO (read)

- [`vapour_read_raster_raw()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_read_raster_int()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_read_raster_dbl()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_read_raster_chr()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_read_raster_hex()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster_raw.md)
  : type safe(r) raster read

- [`vapour_read_raster_block()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_raster_block.md)
  : Read or write raster block

- [`vapour_write_raster_block()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_write_raster_block.md)
  :

  Write data to a block *in an existing file*.

- [`vapour_warp_raster()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_warp_raster.md)
  : Raster warper (reprojection)

- [`vapour_warp_raster_raw()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_warp_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_warp_raster_int()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_warp_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_warp_raster_dbl()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_warp_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_warp_raster_chr()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_warp_raster_raw.md)
  [`vapour_warp_raster_hex()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_warp_raster_raw.md)
  : type safe(r) raster warp

- [`vapour_create_options()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_create.md)
  [`vapour_create()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_create.md)
  : Create raster file

- [`gdal_raster_data()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/gdal_raster_data.md)
  [`gdal_raster_dsn()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/gdal_raster_data.md)
  [`gdal_raster_image()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/gdal_raster_data.md)
  [`gdal_raster_nara()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/gdal_raster_data.md)
  : General raster read and convert

## Vector layers

Inspect layers, geometry columns and summaries.

- [`vapour_layer_names()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_layer_names.md)
  : Read GDAL layer names
- [`vapour_layer_info()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_layer_info.md)
  : Read GDAL layer info
- [`vapour_layer_extent()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_layer_extent.md)
  : Read layer extent
- [`vapour_geom_name()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_geom_name.md)
  : Read geometry column name
- [`vapour_geom_summary()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_geom_summary.md)
  : Summary of available geometry

## Vector geometry and fields

Read geometry, feature identifiers and attribute fields.

- [`vapour_read_geometry_ia()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_geometry.md)
  [`vapour_read_geometry_ij()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_geometry.md)
  [`vapour_read_geometry()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_geometry.md)
  [`vapour_read_geometry_text()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_geometry.md)
  [`vapour_read_extent()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_geometry.md)
  [`vapour_read_type()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_geometry.md)
  : Read GDAL feature geometry
- [`vapour_read_fids()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_fids.md)
  [`vapour_read_names()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_fids.md)
  : Read feature names
- [`vapour_read_fields()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_fields.md)
  [`vapour_read_attributes()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_read_fields.md)
  : Read feature field data
- [`vapour_report_fields()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_report_fields.md)
  [`vapour_report_attributes()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_report_fields.md)
  : Read feature field types.

## CRS, GDAL and configuration

Projection strings, versions, drivers and GDAL config.

- [`vapour_srs_wkt()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_srs_wkt.md)
  : PROJ4 string to WKT
- [`vapour_crs_is_lonlat()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_crs_is_lonlat.md)
  : Is the CRS string representative of angular coordinates
- [`vapour_proj_data()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_proj_data.md)
  : Report on the PROJ data directory in use
- [`vapour_set_config()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_set_config.md)
  [`vapour_get_config()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_set_config.md)
  : Set and query GDAL configuration options
- [`vapour_gdal_version()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/GDAL-library.md)
  [`vapour_proj_version()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/GDAL-library.md)
  [`vapour_all_drivers()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/GDAL-library.md)
  [`vapour_driver()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/GDAL-library.md)
  : GDAL version and drivers.

## Virtual sources

VRT construction and virtual file system listings.

- [`vapour_vrt()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_vrt.md)
  : Virtual raster
- [`vector_vrt()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vector_vrt.md)
  : Vector VRT
- [`buildvrt()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/buildvrt.md)
  : Build vrt, special case "-separate"
- [`vapour_vsi_list()`](https://hypertidy.github.io/vapour/reference/vapour_vsi_list.md)
  : Read GDAL virtual source contents
